chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Shepherd's Cafe and pianist Coot Davis
summary: Sitting in at Shepherd's Cafe with his grandfather on bass, soulful drummer Skinny Thomas and blues pianist Coot Davis.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And there were so many different characters around through that period that I heard play, some fantastic players... Down on Neal Street in Jackson was a cafe called Shepherd's Cafe, and I used to go in there and sit in sometimes with Britt Roseby(?), and my grandfather played in there. The piano player was named Coot Davis, and Skinny Thompson...Thomas playing the drums. Now, he was a very soulful drummer. He didn't know how to read and all that, but he had a great feel on those drums, you know. And my grandfather played the bass.

And Coot Davis...was a fantastic blues piano player. Just fantastic. In fact... You know what I mean when you say "roll" on the piano, how to get the tremolo, really... He could tremolo on that piano stronger than anybody I've ever heard in my life. I mean, he could make that piano just roll. I have never seen anybody or heard anybody before or since who could make that piano like he could make it... Just roll, you know. It was fantastic!
